Read the following fictional engineering brief.

1. The team is comparing three local inference engines on the same battery-powered device. Engine Cedar opens a compact model quickly but decodes slowly, engine Juniper spends longer preparing its model but has steadier generation, and engine Rowan uses more memory in exchange for faster prompt processing. All measurements must distinguish setup, prompt processing, and token generation.

2. The application normally remains open for twenty to forty minutes, although some users close it immediately after one request. A route with expensive setup can therefore be reasonable only when the loaded session is reused. The recommendation should account for both a one-request visit and a longer session without combining their timing boundaries.

3. The device has limited memory and the operating system may reclaim background processes under pressure. Mapped model files, private anonymous allocations, shared pages, runtime workspaces, and the growing key-value cache do not have identical memory semantics. Peak sampled proportional set size and process high-water marks must be labeled rather than treated as interchangeable.

4. Prompt lengths vary substantially. A short request contains only a direct instruction, a medium request includes several pages of notes, and a long request approaches the useful context expected by the application. Token counts differ across model tokenizers even when the exact UTF-8 prompt bytes are identical.

5. Time to first token includes work a user experiences before text appears, while prefill throughput isolates processing of the input tokens. Decode throughput describes the later stream of generated tokens. A runtime that exposes only one combined timing cannot be credited with an invented split between prefill and sampling.

6. The first request can trigger page faults, lazy runtime initialization, cache allocation, or accelerator compilation that later requests avoid. Repeated requests must clear conversation and key-value state while retaining the loaded model session. The report must preserve the first observation separately from the same-session distribution.

7. Thermal conditions are not constant. Sustained generation may heat the phone enough to change clock rates, and charging can change both power and temperature. The operator records the battery and thermal state before and after the campaign and does not describe an unmeasured power value as zero.

8. Outputs are retained so that obvious execution failures remain visible. A nonempty string is not automatically useful: a broken route may emit token identifiers, binary-looking fragments, repeated punctuation, or a short loop. The initial screen asks only whether the exact output looks like sensible text and deliberately avoids a broader quality claim.
